title: Releasing a Learned Policy: Every Check of Phase 38 Run Against One Job, and the First That Fails Named

questions.question: Why is beating the straight line the first requirement?
options: A network that does no better than a line has earned nothing, and the line can be read by a person
Because lines are always worse
Because it is the quickest check to code
Because the line is the expert
questions.explanation: If the network does not beat the baseline, ship the baseline.

questions.question: The DAgger policy: what were its test error, success and handover?
options: 0.01240, 73 percent and 12 percent
0.00022 against the line's 0.01240, 98 percent, and 3.2 percent
0.00056, 95 percent and 5 percent
It was not tested
questions.explanation: Every requirement passed, so it was released.

questions.question: Where did the plain clone fail, and why?
options: At requirement 3 only, since its guard handed over on 12 percent
At requirement 6, it could not be trained again
At requirement 1: on the job's episodes its error, 0.01618, was worse than the line's 0.01240
It passed
questions.explanation: Taught only near the centre, it extrapolates worse than a line. Its guard's 12 percent would have failed it at 3 as well.

questions.question: The DAgger policy given starts within 0.95 m and 1.2 rad failed at requirement 2. What does that say?
options: The policy is bad
The line should be shipped
The job asks for starts some of which no controller can recover from; the policy still beats the line
The guard is broken
questions.explanation: It succeeded on 73 percent. The verdict says the job is the problem, not the network.

questions.question: A network of one hidden unit trained for 2 epochs passed every requirement. Why?
options: The expert is a line clipped at the car's limit, and one tanh unit is almost exactly a clipped line
The check is too easy
Two epochs is always enough
It was lucky with its seed
questions.explanation: A network the size of the task's shape is enough. The line comparison is what shows a small one has earned its place.

questions.question: Why must a released policy carry the data and settings it was trained with?
options: So that it can be trained again, to fix it or to show it was made the way it says
To make the file larger
Because the guard needs the data at run time
So that the test set can be recovered
questions.explanation: A policy that cannot be made again cannot be audited or repaired.
